title: Corner Kick-Out Footwork
description: Corner shooters work on the footwork for a kick-out three: feet behind the line, turned toward the driver, ready to catch and shoot from a pass along the baseline.

content.objective: Hold the corner with the feet behind the line and the body turned to the ball, then catch and shoot without stepping on the line.
content.setup: Driver at the wing; shooter in the corner.
content.organization: Shooter rebounds and becomes the driver.
instructions: The shooter stands in the corner, both feet behind the line, hips open toward the wing.
The driver drives baseline toward the block.
The shooter slides a half-step to stay in the driver's sight line.
The driver kicks the ball out; the shooter catches with the inside foot forward.
Turn the shoulders to the rim and shoot.
coachingPoints: Feet behind the line: check before the pass.
Turn on the catch, not before.
commonMistakes: Stepping on the line and turning a three into a two.
Standing straight-legged and adding a dip.
Drifting toward the driver into the help.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
progressions: Add a defender recovering from the help.
Drift to the corner from the wing on the drive.
variations: Kick out from a middle drive.
Lift to the wing instead of staying in the corner.
successCriteria: Feet behind the line on every catch.
content.gameApplication: The corner three is the shortest three-pointer and the target of most drive-and-kicks.
